clue.text: A plant — if such a variant is one

indicators.note: a variant is a different version, so the three words before it are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: A gardener muses that a certain plant could count as a variant of some other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variant' turns the letters of IF SUCH A into the shrub's name; 'is one' just links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuchsia is a flowering garden shrub with drooping red and purple blooms.

clue.text: Walton's deceptive appearance

explanation.surface: A Walton has a misleading look.
explanation.walkthrough: William Walton, the English composer, wrote an entertainment with this title to poems by Edith Sitwell.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of Walton's 1922 work, and also a false front put on to mislead.

clue.text: Money remitted, say, to cover eggs when upset

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits on top of the second, covering it
say tells us the word for remitted is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: sent means remitted, as money sent by post

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ova is the Latin plural for eggs

explanation.surface: Cash is sent off to insure some eggs in case they get knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'to cover' means sitting on top, and 'upset' means turned upside down; 'say' signals the sound of remitted, not its spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A centavo is a small coin, one hundredth of the peso and similar Latin American currencies.

clue.text: Wild chat after Scotsman builds boat on wheels

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged letters behind the Scottish name

parts.note: Sandy, short for Alexander, is a stock Scottish name

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of chat run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A Scot builds a beach vehicle while chatting excitedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'builds' is only a link; 'Wild' is the anagram signal and 'after' puts the Scottish name first.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a wind-powered wheeled craft with a sail, raced along beaches.

clue.text: Army aid once taken out of air forces

indicators.note: taken out suggests the letters are pulled apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: Military help that was formerly removed from the air force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken out' rearranges ARMY AID ONCE; 'air forces' is a misleading phrase for the forces exerted by air.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the study of how moving air pushes on bodies, so it relates to the pressures of flight.

clue.text: Surrounded by salt water it could be a danger

definitions.note: describes an island, used here to stand for an island nation

indicators.note: the phrase suggests the words beside it might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A warning that being cut off by the sea might be perilous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it could be' rearranges A DANGER; the definition is a description of an island rather than a noun synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenada is a Caribbean island state, a piece of land with the sea all round it.

clue.text: Stick some people swear by?

explanation.surface: A stick that people put their trust in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swear by' suggests trusting something; here it is the old northern English oath 'by gum!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gum is an adhesive used to stick things, and 'by gum' is a mild exclamation of surprise.

clue.text: Join up back in Nepal or New' Guinea

indicators.note: back tells us the hidden letters are read in reverse
in tells us the word lies within the run of clue words

explanation.surface: Enlisting again somewhere in the Himalayas or the South Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' hides LORNE in nepaL OR NEw, and 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to sign up as a member, the same as enlisting.

clue.text: Give him a ring and he'll perform spectacular feats

definitions.text: Give him a ring and he'll perform spectacular feats

parts.words: Give him a ring and he'll perform spectacular feats
parts.note: a ring here is the circus ring in which a tumbler performs, not a phone call

explanation.walkthrough: 'Give him a ring' suggests a phone call; the ring is the circus arena.
explanation.definitionFit: This performer does gymnastic tricks and balancing in the circus.

clue.text: Turn right in narrow passageway it's symbolic

indicators.note: in places the turn and right pieces inside the passageway

parts.note: an alley is a narrow lane between buildings
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Someone turns right in a narrow alley and finds it full of meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' looks like a verb but gives GO, a turn in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegory is a story whose characters stand for deeper meanings.

clue.text: Riddle of sister smothered by fellow instrumentalist

indicators.note: being smothered by something means being covered over by it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: CO is a prefix meaning joint or fellow, as in co-worker
drum is an old word for a drummer, as in a regimental drum
a nun is a religious sister

explanation.surface: A puzzling tale of a nun overwhelmed by another musician in the band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instrumentalist' looks like a whole word for a player; a drum for a drummer is a dated military usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A conundrum is a puzzling question, a synonym of a brain-teaser.

clue.text: Country artist interned by government out east

indicators.note: someone interned is held inside, so the artist goes inside the other piece
out tells us a letter is dropped from the word for government

parts.note: rule means government, as in British rule
E is the compass abbreviation for east
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A painter from the provinces is detained by a regime somewhere abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' is the adjective, as in country life, not a nation; 'out' drops the east letter before 'interned by' does its work.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural means relating to the countryside rather than the town, an adjectival synonym.

clue.text: Record written years after repulse of attack

indicators.note: after places the years abbreviation behind the reversed piece
to repulse is to drive back, so the word for attack is turned backwards

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack

explanation.surface: An account set down long after an assault was beaten off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repulse of' means driving back, so the attack word is read backwards before 'after' adds the years.
explanation.definitionFit: A diary is a daily written log, so it keeps a record of events.

clue.text: American insect larva once dangerous at the end of the fall

definitions.text: once dangerous at the end of the fall

explanation.surface: A bug from America, formerly risky when tumbling to earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the German V-1 flying bomb of the Second World War, nicknamed this in Britain, which exploded when its engine cut out and it fell.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US it names the antlion grub; in wartime Britain it was slang for the V-1 flying bomb, deadly once it came down.

clue.text: Remarkable attitude adopted during trip

indicators.note: something adopted during an event sits within it, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: an outing is a short trip
a stand is a position or attitude taken

explanation.surface: A notable stance taken on an excursion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attitude' is a position taken on an issue, and 'adopted during' sets it within the trip.
explanation.definitionFit: It means exceptionally good, so it is a synonym of striking or excellent.

clue.text: Animal about to deceive particular old snake

indicators.note: about here means around, so the animal goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a boar is a wild pig
to con is to swindle or deceive
strict and particular both mean fussy about rules or detail

explanation.surface: Some beast is about to fool a fussy old serpent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal' looks like the definition but supplies BOAR, which goes 'about' CON + STRICT + O.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large South American serpent that kills prey by squeezing it.

clue.text: Curl up with kitten in centre of porch, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged in some other order
the centre of a five-letter word is its third letter

explanation.surface: A cat lover curls up in a porch with a kitten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges KITTEN + IN + R, the 'centre of' PORCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To interknit is to intertwine, so it means to twist together with something.

clue.text: Branch temporarily unattracted by hunting expedition

parts.note: having gone off something means losing interest in it, perhaps for a while
a shoot is an outing to hunt game birds

explanation.surface: Someone loses interest for a while in a grouse-hunting trip.
explanation.definitionFit: An offshoot is a side stem or spin-off, a branch from the main growth.

clue.text: New firm motto I meet now and then

indicators.note: new suggests the following letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone encounters a company's fresh slogan every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges all fourteen letters of FIRM MOTTO I MEET.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean occasionally, at irregular intervals.

clue.text: Moving about a little during examination

indicators.note: during puts the small amount inside the examination word

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
a bit is a little

explanation.surface: Someone fidgets slightly in a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' here means circling, as a satellite does.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbital describes travel on a circular path round a body such as a planet.

clue.text: Set-up in masculine environment makes us sort of cross

indicators.note: an environment surrounds, so the masculine word goes around the other piece

parts.note: male means masculine

indicators.note: up suggests the letters of set are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A setting in a men-only place makes us angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set-up' reads as a noun but splits into fodder plus anagram signal; 'cross' is not anger here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maltese cross has four arms broadening outwards, each with a notched end.

clue.text: Relative importance of sculptor's oeuvre out east

indicators.note: out tells us a letter is dropped from the sculptor's works

parts.note: statues are a sculptor's body of work
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Critics weigh a sculptor's output in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes E from STATUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is standing or rank, a person's position relative to others.

clue.text: Minister and colonel in, vehicle reversed by college official

indicators.note: by here means beside, putting the two pieces next to each other
reversed tells us the vehicle word is read backwards

parts.note: a bus is a road vehicle

indicators.note: in tells us the colonel abbreviation goes inside the official

parts.note: a dean is a senior officer of a college
CO is the abbreviation for commanding officer, typically a colonel

explanation.surface: A clergyman and an army colonel ride in a bus driven backwards by a university don.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'in' marks off the container from the reversed vehicle; 'by' means beside.
explanation.definitionFit: A subdeacon is a cleric in minor orders, one who ministers below a deacon.

clue.text: In good time, ultimately, like Lear's uncle

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so we take the closing letter of like

parts.note: Edward Lear, the Victorian nonsense poet, wrote of My Uncle Arly

explanation.surface: Punctually, as befits an elderly relative of King Lear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lear's' suggests Shakespeare's king; it is Edward Lear's poem 'Incidents in the Life of My Uncle Arly'.
explanation.definitionFit: It means before the due time, so punctual or ahead of schedule.

clue.text: Grant new lease to soldiers, adding a restriction

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a let is a hindrance, as in the legal phrase without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: A landlord renews a tenancy for some troops but imposes a condition.
explanation.walkthrough: LET as an obstacle survives in 'without let or hindrance' and in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: To relet is to rent a property out again, granting a fresh lease.

clue.text: Poor shot striking with hesitation

parts.note: workers out on strike are said to be out
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A marksman misses after hesitating while taking aim.
explanation.walkthrough: In archery and shooting this is a hit on the outermost ring of the target, a low-scoring shot. 'striking' means on strike, not hitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot landing in the target's outer ring scores little, so it counts as a weak effort.

clue.text: Co-ordination achieved by dressing carefully

parts.note: dressing in drill means soldiers adjusting their positions so the ranks are in a straight line, not putting on clothes

explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' suggests clothes; on the parade ground to dress is to line up the ranks evenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranging items in a straight line or proper relation to each other gives orderly positioning.

clue.text: Old silver superior in the past

indicators.note: superior means above, so in a down answer the silver symbol sits on top

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Antique silver was better back then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'superior' places AG above O in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ago means before now, a synonym of previously.

clue.text: Cry briefly, however, when embracing friend

indicators.note: embracing means holding round, so the shortened word goes around the friend
briefly means shortened, the informal clipped spelling of the word

parts.note: though can mean however, as in he left early though
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Someone shouts out quickly, yet while hugging a pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' gives the informal clipped spelling of the word for however, and 'embracing' puts it round the friend.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the shout that fox hunters give on sighting the quarry.

clue.text: Assembles firearm belonging to a woman

parts.note: gat is old American slang for a pistol
hers means owned by a female

explanation.surface: Someone puts together a gun that is a lady's property.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather is to bring together or collect, so it is a synonym of convene in the transitive sense.
